 Zach LaVine accounted for 37 points (13-of-25 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), two rebounds, five assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Grizzlies.
 After scoring 50 points in Sacramento’s first two games, LaVine recorded his first 30-point game of the season on Sunday. He was efficient, shooting 52 percent from the field. Sunday’s performance was an excellent way for LaVine to end Week 1, as the Kings begin a three-game Week 2 in San Antonio on Tuesday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Zach LaVine with 22 points (6-of-15 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), five rebounds, an assist, two steals, a block, and three 3-pointers on Friday. 
 This is basically what you signed up for when you took Zach LaVine in the later rounds of redraft leagues and you should be pretty happy after this performance. Getting to the line seven times and hitting all seven is really good. You obviously wish he were a bit more efficient from the field, but it’s hard to complain when you get that kind of scoring.

 Guard 
 #8 
 Zach LaVine recorded 28 points (10-of-19 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), four rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Clippers. 
 After injuries limited him to 39 games in his first full season with the Kings, LaVine looked completely healthy on Wednesday. Without him and fellow veteran Domantas Sabonis, the Kings would have fared worse, but they still lost the opener 121-96. As long as he stays healthy, LaVine should return to being a reliable fantasy asset. The question is whether a good first half of the season would convince a contending team to acquire him before the February trade deadline. 
 Zach LaVine 
 SAC 
 Guard 
 #8 
 According to Locked on Kings’ James Ham, the Kings are not interested in exercising the waive-and-stretch provision on Zach LaVine. 
 In an unsurprising move, LaVine exercised his player option for the 2026-27 season, as he is set to make just over $49 million. Given the youth of Sacramento’s roster, the veteran guard’s role for next season is unknown. What is reportedly known is that the front office is not willing to put its long-term financial future at risk by waiving LaVine and stretching his contract. The contract makes LaVine a challenging player to move, which would not have been the case had he not picked up the player option. When at his best, LaVine can offer middle-round value in standard fantasy leagues. However, due to the Kings’ current position as a rebuilding team and LaVine coming off a season in which he played 39 games, his draft value may be knocked down a few rounds. 
 Zach LaVine

 Zach LaVine has reportedly decided to opt into the final season of his contract. 
 LaVine opting into the final season of his contract is unsurprising, as he will make a base salary of $49 million, a figure he was unlikely to match in free agency. The question now is where he fits within the Kings’ rebuild. Between the selections of Nique Clifford and Maxime Raynaud in last summer’s draft, and Darius Acuff Jr., Alex Karaban and Emanuel Sharpe last week, the franchise is clearly looking to build around its younger players. LaVine getting his usual offensive volume likely would not mesh with that, but his contract may be challenging to move if the Kings wanted to go that route.

 NBA insider Chris Haynes reports that Zach LaVine (hand) will undergo season-ending surgery. 
 Due to a right fifth finger injury, LaVine missed Sacramento’s final three games before the All-Star break. Apparently, the injury is more serious than the Kings may have let on, as the guard will reportedly undergo season-ending surgery after the break. LaVine, who appeared in 39 games and averaged 19.2 points, 2.8 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 0.7 steals and 2.5 three-pointers, has a player option for next season worth nearly $49 million. As for how his absence affects the Kings in the short term, rookie Nique Clifford has moved into the starting lineup and should remain there for the rest of the season.

 Zach LaVine accumulated 35 points (13-of-26 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Wizards. 
 After totaling 34 points in his first two games back from injury, LaVine surpassed that number on Sunday. Given the matchup, with the Wizards having the youngest team in the NBA and also headed for the draft lottery, it’s unsurprising that he had a big night. However, with the trade deadline on the horizon, it’s worth questioning what LaVine’s future will be. The size of his contract may make it difficult for the Kings to find a trade partner, and if he doesn’t get moved, how much will he play after the deadline? Sacramento plays three games in Week 16, two of which are after Thursday’s trade deadline. 
 Zach LaVine 
 SAC 
 Guard 
 #8 
 Zach LaVine returned to the starting lineup on Friday and finished with 17 points (5-of-9 FGs), four rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer against the Celtics. 
 LaVine came off the bench in his return from a two-game absence on Thursday, and he returned to the starting lineup 24 hours later. He scored 17 points in both games, though he was more efficient in this one, even if the result on the scoreboard was the same. LaVine’s name will be floated around in trade rumors as the deadline approaches, but until then, he’ll remain a decent scoring option, even if he hasn’t been able to score as much as he typically does in recent weeks.

 Precious Achiuwa tallied 12 points (6-of-13 FGs, 0-of-6 FTs), 10 rebounds, two steals and three blocks in Sunday’s loss to the Grizzlies.
 The Kings were without Keegan Murray (ankle) for Sunday’s game, so Achiuwa made a spot start. While his foul shooting was a disaster, the positives outweighed that negative in terms of the Kings forward’s production. Achiuwa played 39 minutes against the Grizzlies and recorded a double-double with five “stocks.” Sacramento plays three games in Week 2, starting with the Spurs on Tuesday, and Achiuwa would be a worthwhile pickup if Murray remains out.

 Isaiah Stewart tallied 13 points (4-of-8 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal, two blocks and two three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Kings.
 The Grizzlies gave Zach Edey the night off, so Beef Stew was inserted into the starting lineup. Stewart’s value was his defense and three-point shooting, but he played just 22 minutes. He missed most of the preseason with a sprained ankle, which likely factored into his playing time. Edey should be back for Monday’s game against the Jazz, which would push Stewart to the bench.

 Ty Jerome amassed 31 points (8-of-17 FGs, 14-of-14 FTs), four rebounds, six assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Sunday’s win over the Kings.
 For those who believed Jerome would cool off after scoring 73 points in the Grizzlies’ first two games, that didn’t happen on Sunday. He did most of his damage inside the arc, making 7 of 11 two-point attempts and shooting 14-for-14 from the foul line. Add in the assists, and it was another excellent night for those rostering Jerome, one of the best players in fantasy basketball so far. The Grizzlies play three games in Week 2, starting with the Jazz on Monday.

 Jaylen Brown accounted for 16 points (5-of-20 FGs, 4-of-8 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, one block and two three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Pistons.
 After a strong start in his first three appearances for the 76ers, Brown cooled off on Sunday. He shot 3-of-14 from inside the arc against the Pistons, and many of those misses came in the paint. There’s no need to lose any sleep over Brown’s performance against the Pistons, as the overall track record has been good. He’ll look to bounce back on Wednesday against the Pacers.

 Back in the lineup after sitting out Saturday’s win over the Bucks, James played 33 minutes on Sunday. Some of those minutes came at center, as the 76ers did not have Joel Embiid. James had a decent night, but he wasn’t as impactful as many fantasy managers likely hoped in the 76ers’ final game of Week 1.

 Tyrese Maxey (head) finished Sunday’s loss to the Pistons with 29 points (11-of-24 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, three steals, one block and one three-pointer.
 Maxey and the 76ers were playing their third game in four days. With LeBron James (Saturday) and Joel Embiid (Sunday) each missing a game, the 76ers’ star point guard had to shoulder a heavier workload. Despite that, Maxey still recorded an efficient stat line to end Week 1. There was an injury scare when he collided with Detroit’s John Collins in the fourth quarter, but Maxey was fine. Philadelphia plays three games in Week 2, starting with the Pacers on Wednesday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 John Collins notched 16 points (7-of-15 FGs), 11 rebounds, two blocks and two three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the 76ers.
 Jalen Duren’s hamstring injury wouldn’t affect Collins’ place in the Pistons’ starting lineup. However, the All-Star center’s absence meant Collins would sometimes be the biggest Piston on the floor. Philadelphia didn’t have Joel Embiid on Sunday, which made the paint a bit more manageable for Detroit. But that shouldn’t take away from Collins’ double-double and blocked shots. Collins is already rostered in 80 percent of Yahoo leagues, and the Duren injury raises his fantasy ceiling.
